heading_pairs.heading: A four-week trial shows when to look closer
heading_pairs.following: Temperature sensors in six classrooms can tell a property manager when the air dropped below a chosen limit — and nothing about why anyone felt cold. This is what a four-week trial at one school established, what it did not measure, and what to record before the controls are changed.

heading_pairs.heading: Fourteen of 120 lesson periods held a reading below 20 degrees
heading_pairs.following: Values were logged every five minutes for the whole period.

heading_pairs.heading: Ventilation, draught and radiant heat went unrecorded
heading_pairs.following: A sensor reports the temperature of the air at the point where it is mounted, and nothing else about the room.

heading_pairs.heading: A count of periods is not a measure of how cold it got
heading_pairs.following: The report does not say how long any reading stayed under the limit, and it does not say whether the pupils were cold.

heading_pairs.heading: Pair the readings with usage times before changing the controls
heading_pairs.following: Which lesson periods to examine, then, is the narrower question these four weeks answer.
